title: Early Havana childhood and the fire in the solar
summary: He recalls happy Havana, his father selling water glasses, setting fire to the stock, and living in the Jesus Maria solar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh huh. Macho, what do you remember about your early childhood in Havana?
Well, Havana was so musical, so gay - I mean, so full of life, that I, I don't know, I never had a moment that I, that was a sad moment because that was very happy, very happy era.
Okay, do you remember anything, let's say, from the age five? Do you remember when you were five years old?
Oh, when I was five my father was selling glasses, they was coming from Europe.

Eye - no - water-glasses; and you know, was a big case with a lot of stuff, with some kind of thing in order to preserve the glasses and I guess I got a match and I set a fire to all of them, Where we lived, that was completely destroyed by a fire so everybody hit me in the neighborhood.
Macho, did you live in one of the solares or did you live in an apartment?
No, first I lived in a solar, you know, one of those .....
Okay, do you remember the name of the solar and what district?
It was the Jesus Maria. They called it
el solar de los carretones. The, you know, the buggy - buggy solar.
